questions.question: What is a critical band briefly? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What is a critical band briefly?
  • A critical band is the frequency bandwidth of the ear within which sounds mask each other.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: How does reverberation affect perceived distance of a sound? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• How does reverberation affect perceived distance of a sound?
  • More reverberation makes a sound appear farther away.

questions.question: Define dynamic range. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Define dynamic range.
  • Dynamic range is the difference between the loudest and softest sound levels in a system.

questions.question: Explain briefly why sound is treated as a pressure wave in air. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain briefly why sound is treated as a pressure wave in air.
  • Sound travels as alternating compressions and rarefactions of air pressure.

questions.question: What SPL value is commonly cited as the threshold of pain? / [CO2] [2x10 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• What SPL value is commonly cited as the threshold of pain?
  • The threshold of pain is approximately 120 dB SPL.

questions.question: Explain occupational exposure standards for sound (briefly cite typical d B/time limits) and their rationale. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain occupational exposure standards for sound (briefly cite typical dB/time limits) and their
  • rationale.
  • Safe limit: 85 dB for 8 hours
  • Every 3 dB increase halves safe exposure time
  • Purpose: hearing protection
  • Prevents NIHL (Noise-Induced Hearing Loss)
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain ITD and ILD cues and how they jointly provide horizontal localization information. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain ITD and ILD cues and how they jointly provide horizontal localization Information.
  • ITD: Time difference between ears
  • ILD: Level difference between ears
  • Used for horizontal localization
  • Works mainly for mid–high frequencies
  • Brain combines both cues .
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain how masking and noise floor affect useful dynamic range in recordings. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how masking and noise floor affect useful dynamic range in recordings.
  • Noise floor hides low-level signals
  • Masking occurs when loud sound hides weaker sound
  • Reduces usable dynamic range
  • Affects clarity in recordings
  • Controlled by gain staging
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Compare the harmonic content of sine, square, triangle and sawtooth waves, and explain why they sound different. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Compare the harmonic content of sine, square, triangle and sawtooth waves, and explain why
  • they sound different.
  • Sine: Only fundamental
  • Square: Odd harmonics
  • Triangle: Weak odd harmonics
  • Sawtooth: All harmonics
  • Timbre difference due to harmonics .
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain how alignment level and operating level differ and why both matter. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how alignment level and operating level differ and why both matter.
  • Alignment: Reference calibration level
  • Operating level: Actual working level
  • Prevents distortion
  • Maintains signal-to-noise ratio
  • Ensures system compatibility .

questions.question: Describe the Doppler effect and derive the qualitative pitch change when a source moves toward a listener. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the Doppler effect and derive the qualitative pitch change when a source moves toward a
  • listener.
  • Change in frequency due to motion
  • Approaching source: higher pitch
  • Receding source: lower pitch
  • Used in sirens & radar
  • Based on relative velocity .
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe the functions of the outer, middle and inner ear in the chain of acoustic transduction. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the functions of the outer, middle and inner ear in the chain of acoustic transduction.
  • Outer: Collects sound
  • Middle: Amplifies vibrations
  • Inner: Converts vibrations to nerve impulses
  • Ear ossicles named
  • Cochlea function included .
